intro: Buying a home in Nebraska requires more than finding a property within your preferred price range. Local property taxes, mortgage interest rates, homeowners insurance and ongoing maintenance expenses all influence how much you can comfortably afford.

Our free Nebraska mortgage calculator helps you estimate your monthly housing payment using your home price, down payment, interest rate and loan term. Whether you're purchasing in Omaha, Lincoln, Grand Island, Kearney or a smaller Nebraska community, compare financing options before committing to a property.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Nebraska?

blocks.markdown:
A $240,000 Nebraska home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,151.14.

An illustrative monthly housing payment breakdown is shown below.
This example assumes no private mortgage insurance or HOA fees. Property taxes, insurance premiums and interest rates are illustrative rather than verified statewide averages.

Nebraska offers housing opportunities across metropolitan neighborhoods, suburban developments, agricultural regions and smaller communities.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Nebraska QuickFacts](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/NE/POP715223), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $238,600 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among households with mortgages were $1,736, while approximately 66.5% of occupied housing units were owner-occupied.

These historical statistics include homeowners who purchased properties under different market conditions. They do not represent current mortgage offers or property asking prices.

Homes near major employment centers in Omaha and Lincoln may have different purchase prices from properties in western Nebraska.

Consider transportation, local taxes, insurance and maintenance expenses when comparing homes in different communities.

sections.heading: How to Use the Nebraska Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Enter the expected purchase price of your property and the amount you intend to contribute as a down payment.

Select your preferred repayment period and enter the annual mortgage interest rate quoted by your lender.

If you have not received a mortgage quote, consult [Freddie Mac's mortgage market survey](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms) for a national benchmark.

Next, include annual property taxes, homeowners insurance premiums and applicable association fees.

Add private mortgage insurance if your conventional financing requires it.

Review the estimated monthly housing payment and experiment with different purchase prices, repayment periods and down payments.

The amortization schedule also shows how your outstanding loan balance decreases over time and how much interest you could pay.

Our national Mortgage Calculator allows you to compare similar financing arrangements outside Nebraska.

sections.heading: How Nebraska Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Property taxes are an important consideration when establishing a Nebraska homebuying budget.

According to the [Nebraska Department of Revenue's property assessment guidance](https://revenue.nebraska.gov/about/frequently-asked-questions/nebraska-property-assessment-faqs), ordinary residential real estate is assessed at or near its full actual value.

Agricultural and horticultural land uses different assessment rules.

County assessors establish property valuations, while local government budgets and tax levies influence the amount homeowners pay.

### Nebraska property tax calculation example

Suppose a residential property has an assessed value of $240,000 and a hypothetical combined property tax rate of $1.75 per $100 of assessed value.

If applicable property tax credits reduce the annual bill by $300, the remaining liability would be $3,900, equivalent to $325 per month.

The tax rate and credit amount are hypothetical. Actual liabilities depend on local levies, property valuations and applicable state relief provisions.

### Nebraska property tax credits

Nebraska homeowners may benefit from two state-funded credits that directly reduce their property tax bills:

- Real Property Tax Credit.
- School District Property Tax Relief Credit.

The [Nebraska Department of Revenue's property tax credit directory](https://revenue.nebraska.gov/PAD/Property-Tax-Credits) publishes information about these credits.

Nebraska also provides a separate income tax credit associated with qualifying community college property taxes.

Review the state's [property tax credit FAQs](https://revenue.nebraska.gov/about/frequently-asked-questions/nebraska-property-tax-credit-faqs) to distinguish credits claimed through income tax returns from reductions appearing directly on property tax statements.

Avoid subtracting credits again if they are already reflected in the property's net annual tax bill.

### Nebraska homestead exemption

Nebraska provides property tax relief to qualifying older homeowners, individuals with eligible disabilities and certain disabled veterans or surviving spouses.

The [Nebraska homestead exemption program](https://revenue.nebraska.gov/PAD/homestead-exemption) may exempt part or all of a qualifying residence's taxable value.

Some eligibility categories have income and property valuation restrictions.

This exemption is not automatically available to every homeowner. Contact your county assessor to confirm eligibility, documentation requirements and filing deadlines.

Nebraska properties can experience severe thunderstorms, tornadoes, hail, flooding and winter weather.

Insurance premiums depend on construction materials, replacement costs, roof condition, location and selected coverage.

Request property-specific insurance quotes before completing your purchase.

### Wind and hail insurance

Roof coverage deserves particular attention when comparing policies.

The [Nebraska Department of Insurance's storm preparedness guidance](https://doi.nebraska.gov/storm-dont-wait-until-its-too-late) recommends reviewing wind and hail deductibles and ensuring that coverage is sufficient to rebuild your home.

Some policies use percentage-based deductibles.

For example, a 2% deductible on $250,000 in dwelling coverage would represent $5,000 in potential out-of-pocket costs for an applicable covered claim.

Maintain emergency savings to cover deductibles and repairs.

### Flood insurance

Standard homeowners insurance generally excludes flooding.

Properties near rivers, streams and low-lying areas may require separate coverage.

Consult the [Nebraska Department of Insurance's flood insurance guidance](https://doi.nebraska.gov/flood-insurance-101) and investigate your property's location through the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home).

Include additional insurance premiums in the calculator where applicable.
The following estimates assume a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed annual interest rate and a 30-year mortgage.

These figures exclude property taxes, homeowners insurance, PMI and association fees.

Compare complete monthly housing expenses instead of relying exclusively on principal and interest.

The Nebraska Investment Finance Authority, commonly known as NIFA, offers mortgage financing and purchase assistance through participating lenders.

### First Home and Homebuyer Assistance programs

The [NIFA First Home program](https://www.nifa.org/lenders-realtors/first-home) provides mortgage financing for eligible first-time buyers.

Borrowers who need additional help with upfront expenses can investigate the [Homebuyer Assistance Program](https://www.nifa.org/lenders-realtors/homebuyer-assistance).

This arrangement combines a primary mortgage with a second mortgage of up to 5% of the property's purchase price.

The second mortgage has a ten-year repayment period and a fixed interest rate of 1%.

For example, assistance equal to 5% of a $240,000 purchase price would amount to $12,000. Repaying that loan over ten years at 1% would cost approximately $105.12 monthly.

Include this additional payment when evaluating your total housing expenses.

### Welcome Home program

The [NIFA Welcome Home program](https://www.nifa.org/homebuyers-renters/welcome-home) is available to qualifying first-time and repeat homebuyers.

Its published limits, effective July 13, 2026, include a household income ceiling of $182,800 and purchase price limits of $485,500 for one-unit properties and $607,000 for two-unit properties.

Welcome Home Assistance is also available to eligible applicants needing help with down payment and closing expenses.

Confirm current financing terms and eligibility with a participating lender.

Conventional mortgages offer flexible repayment periods and down payment arrangements for borrowers meeting lender requirements.

FHA-insured financing may provide an alternative for households with limited upfront savings.

Eligible military borrowers can investigate [VA home loan programs](https://www.va.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans/).

Buyers considering rural properties may also qualify for [USDA Rural Development housing programs](https://www.rd.usda.gov/).

Properties containing agricultural acreage, outbuildings or commercial farming operations may require specialized financing. Confirm property eligibility before relying on a standard residential mortgage estimate.

A shorter repayment period can substantially reduce your total interest expenses.

For a $192,000 mortgage at the same illustrative 6% interest rate, a 15-year loan would require approximately $1,620.21 monthly in principal and interest, compared with $1,151.14 for a 30-year loan.

The shorter term requires approximately $469 more each month but allows you to repay the mortgage considerably sooner.

Use the calculator to compare repayment periods while keeping enough money available for property taxes, insurance, repairs and other financial commitments.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Nebraska?

blocks.markdown:
Start with reliable monthly take-home income and subtract existing financial obligations.

Our [Nebraska Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/nebraska-paycheck-calculator/) can help estimate after-tax earnings, while our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) can help evaluate outstanding borrowing commitments.

Consider transportation costs, winter heating, property maintenance and regular savings contributions.

Rural properties may also require private well maintenance, septic servicing and access road repairs.

Review the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/) when comparing mortgage offers and upfront financing expenses.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $240,000 Nebraska home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year repayment period, principal and interest would be approximately $1,151.14 monthly. Taxes, insurance and applicable fees increase the total housing payment.

### How are Nebraska residential property taxes calculated?

Ordinary residential property is assessed at or near its full actual value. Applicable local tax levies determine the initial tax liability, with adjustments for qualifying exemptions and property tax credits.

### Does Nebraska offer down payment assistance?

Yes. NIFA's Homebuyer Assistance Program offers qualifying borrowers a second mortgage of up to 5% of the purchase price, repayable over ten years at 1% interest. Additional assistance options and eligibility requirements apply.

Use our Nebraska mortgage calculator to compare purchase prices, down payments and financing arrangements before making an offer.

Replace illustrative taxes and insurance premiums with verified property-specific estimates. Understanding your complete housing expenses can help you choose a Nebraska property that supports your long-term financial goals.
